name: Light Chalcedony Yellow
lede: Light Chalcedony Yellow is a light greenish yellow from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, filed again by name in the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary, and named after the mineral chalcedony rather than a flower or dye.

sections.title: A mineral-named Ridgway tone
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carries this swatch on plate XVII, hue 25′, tone d [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary files the exact name "Light Chalcedony Yellow" under block 101, "light greenish yellow" [2]. The name builds "light" onto [[chalcedony-yellow]], after chalcedony, the waxy quartz that can carry this pale tint [1].

In our color library its closest neighbor is [[primrose-yellow]], about 2.7 units away and duller, followed by [[barium-yellow]] at 3.0 units, close enough to pass for the same color [3]. [[light-green-yellow]] sits 3.3 units off and more vivid [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings matches this tone in 189 of them, about 0.79 percent, as photographed, more common than 61 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in the 1400s, present in 6 of the 945 paintings we have from that century, 1.3 times the rate its museums' own baseline would predict [4].

Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 51 percent of its 114 clearly-ranked appearances [4]. It shares canvases with Dark Olive-Buff more than chance, a lift of 3.2 [4]. The earliest dated match is 1415, 497 years before the name's first 1912 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an old photograph, not proof of the name's age [4]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [4].

origin.named_after: the modifier "light" plus [[chalcedony-yellow]], after the mineral chalcedony
